title: Fiberwise relative-colimit lifting across a cocartesian relative join
statement: Use [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], relative diagrams of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone], relative joins of [def-coef-infinity-relative-join], and cocartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $u:K\to C$ be a cocartesian fibration of quasicategories and $p:D\to B$ an isofibration of quasicategories (an inner fibration lifting equivalence edges with specified source). Let $J=K\star_C C$, $f:K\to D$ and $g:J\to B$ satisfy $pf=gi_K$ exactly. Suppose that for every $c\in C$ there is a $p$-colimit diagram $v_c:K_c^{\triangleright}\to D$ with $v_c|_{K_c}=f|_{K_c}$ and $pv_c=gj_c$ exactly, where $K_c=K\times_C\{c\}$ and $j_c$ is its fiber-cone map into $J$. Then there is a functor $\bar f:J\to D$ with $\bar f i_K=f$ and $p\bar f=g$ exactly such that $\bar f j_c$ is a $p$-colimit diagram for every $c$. This imposes no condition on preservation of colimits by fiber transport and no existence of any other colimits in $D$. All objects are small in a fixed sufficiently large universe.

source.place: Proposition 7.3.4.7, implication (2) to (1), with Proposition 7.3.4.3 (02ZP) identifying the fiber cones. No separate quasicategory assertion is needed here. Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags. Read online; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Choose one of the assumed diagrams $v_c$ for each vertex $c$ of $C$. Let $\pi:J\to C$ be the projection in [def-coef-infinity-relative-join], and put $C^{(0)}=\operatorname{sk}_0C$, the simplicial subset of all degenerate simplices of vertices. In each degree it is the disjoint union of the constant simplices at the distinct vertices. The degreewise relative-join formula identifies $\pi^{-1}(\{c\})$ with $K_c\star\Delta^0=K_c^{\triangleright}$: the common base simplex is constant at $c$, so the old block lies in $K_c$ and the new block is the unique simplex of the point. Distinct such fibers are disjoint. Thus $A_0=i_K(K)\cup\pi^{-1}(C^{(0)})$ is obtained by adjoining the separate fiber cones to $K$ along $K_c$. Define $F_0:A_0\to D$ by $f$ on $K$ and $v_c$ on each cone. These maps agree on their entire intersections because $v_c|_{K_c}=f|_{K_c}$. Gluing degreewise gives a simplicial map, and $pF_0=g|_{A_0}$ since these equalities hold on every piece. In particular every vertex fiber cone is already fixed exactly.

source.place: Lemma 7.3.4.6, amalgamating the chosen fiber cones over the zero skeleton.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells] to the inclusion of the empty simplicial set into $C$. After its dimension-zero stage it gives $C^{(0)}$; write $C^{(r)}$ for the stage containing all cells of dimension at most $r$. For $r\geq1$, the next step is the pushout of $\partial\Delta^r\hookrightarrow\Delta^r$ indexed by the nondegenerate $r$-simplices $\sigma$ of $C$, and $\bigcup_r C^{(r)}=C$. Put $A_r=i_K(K)\cup\pi^{-1}(C^{(r)})$. For each such $\sigma$ put $Y_\sigma=J\times_C\Delta^r$, $X_\sigma=K\times_C\Delta^r$, and $M_\sigma=i_{X_\sigma}(X_\sigma)\cup(Y_\sigma\times_{\Delta^r}\partial\Delta^r)$. Then $A_r$ is the pushout of the maps $M_\sigma\hookrightarrow Y_\sigma$ along their maps into $A_{r-1}$. To verify this, pull back the base cell-pushout in each degree: a simplex over the old base is already in $\pi^{-1}(C^{(r-1)})$; every other simplex has the unique new base-cell representative of that pushout. Its choice of simplex in $J$ is unchanged. Adjoining the whole copy of $K$ puts the entire $X_\sigma$ in the attaching domain, so a new simplex in this copy is identified with its already prescribed simplex of $K$. These are precisely the relations of the displayed pushout, and they commute with the simplicial operators. This argument does not require $\sigma$ to be injective on vertices.

source.place: Skeletal expansion of the reduction to one simplex in Lemma 7.3.4.5, used in Lemma 7.3.4.6; the cell presentation is Kerodon 0077.

proof.text: For a base cell $\sigma:\Delta^r\to C$, the pullback $X_\sigma\to\Delta^r$ is a cocartesian fibration in the sense of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Indeed any inner-horn lifting problem projects to one for $u$, and its filler together with the specified simplex of $\Delta^r$ gives a pullback filler. A cocartesian lift in $K$ of the image of a base edge, paired with that edge, is cocartesian in $X_\sigma$: every defining outer-horn lifting problem projects to the one for that lift, and its filler again pairs with the given base simplex. Since $\Delta^r$ fills inner horns (it is the nerve of the ordered set, where a compatible chain is its filler), the same inner-horn argument shows $X_\sigma$ is a quasicategory. Moreover [def-coef-infinity-relative-join] identifies $Y_\sigma$ with $X_\sigma\star_{\Delta^r}\Delta^r$ over $\Delta^r$. Explicitly an $m$-simplex is a time cut $[m]\to[1]$, a base simplex $\tau:\Delta^m\to\Delta^r$, and an old-block simplex of $K$ lying over the corresponding restriction of $\sigma\tau$. Giving that old block together with the restriction of $\tau$ is exactly an old block of $X_\sigma$. Pure old and pure new blocks obey the same rule. Restriction and repetition of these lists commute with this identification. It also identifies $M_\sigma$ with the domain of the local boundary-extension lemma and its vertex-zero cone with the original cone at $\sigma(0)$.

source.place: Degreewise base-change identification and horn checks needed for the one-simplex reduction of 02ZR.

proof.text: Inductively suppose $F_{r-1}:A_{r-1}\to D$ extends $F_0$, restricts to $f$ on $K$, and satisfies $pF_{r-1}=g|_{A_{r-1}}$. Pull it back to $M_\sigma$ for each nondegenerate $r$-cell. Together with $g|_{Y_\sigma}$ this is an exactly commuting lifting square. Since $r\geq1$, every vertex of $\Delta^r$, in particular vertex zero, belongs to its boundary. The restriction to the entire vertex-zero cone is therefore the previously fixed $v_{\sigma(0)}$, with its assumed $p$-colimit property. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-relative-join-simplex-extension] using the cocartesian fibration and the identifications of Step 3, and the original isofibration $p$. Obtain a map on $Y_\sigma$ agreeing with the given map on all of $M_\sigma$ and lying over $g$ exactly. Choose these fillers for the small set of cells and glue them with $F_{r-1}$ using the pushout of Step 2. They agree on the whole attaching domains, so this gives $F_r:A_r\to D$ with the same inductive properties and $F_r|_{A_{r-1}}=F_{r-1}$. The base case is Step 1. No transition functor has been required to preserve a colimit.

source.place: Lemma 7.3.4.5 for each positive-dimensional base cell, preserving the already chosen fiber cones as in 7.3.4.6.

proof.text: Because the base filtration is exhaustive, every simplex of $J$ lies in some $A_r$. Define $\bar f$ on that simplex by $F_r$ there. Compatibility of the extensions makes this independent of $r$, and all simplicial identities hold at a common finite stage. Hence $\bar f:J\to D$ is a simplicial map with $\bar f i_K=f$ and $p\bar f=g$ exactly. Every fiber cone is contained in $A_0$, so $\bar f j_c=v_c$ as a whole simplicial diagram. It is consequently a $p$-colimit diagram by the choice of $v_c$. This proves precisely the requested conclusion without any appeal to global left Kan extension or to colimit-preserving transport.

source.place: Union of the compatible skeletal extensions; concludes Lemma 7.3.4.6 and the fiber-cone conclusion of Proposition 7.3.4.7.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 7.3.4.6, expanded by the relative skeletal filtration and the positive-dimensional simplex case of Lemma 7.3.4.5 (02ZR). Online sources read; archival copies WANTED.
